out_items.name: Person in charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

violations.title: Permit to Operate Required
violations.observation: The food establishment's Permit to Operate is no longer valid due to expiration of the permit. No person shall operate a food establishment unless that person possesses a valid permit issued by the Health Department. Prior to inspection, EHS observed that food establishment permit was expired.
violations.corrective_action: To obtain a current Permit to Operate, contact the Health Department at (703) 246-2201 within 48 hours to make payment of the permit renewal fee. You may provide payment by cash, check, or credit card. Failure to pay the permit renewal fee and obtain a current Permit to Operate within 48 hours may lead to further enforcement actions by the Health Department including immediate closure. CFM contacted appropriate corporate contact, who then immediately renewed food establishment permit. Please post 2026 food establishment permit once received.

out_items.name: Hands clean and properly washed

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands. The food employee changed gloves and did not wash hands before putting new gloves on, as required.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. The EHS discussed this with the manager and the manager discussed it with the employee and the employee washed her hands.

out_items.name: Food-contact surfaces cleaned and sanitized

violations.title: Before Use After Cleaning
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment were not observed sanitized: 1) FOOD BLENDER AND COMPONENTS OBSERVED RINSED AT A FOOD PREP SINK; NOT WASHED OR SANITIZED.
violations.corrective_action: All utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use and after cleaning. EHS DISCUSSED WITH MANAGEMENT AND HE HAD HER TAKE IT TO THE DISH MACHINE.

violations.title: Non-TCS Food Contact Surface, Clean per Manufacturer
violations.observation: Observed the interior of the ice machine in need of cleaning.
violations.corrective_action: Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is NOT time/temperature control for safety food such as ice bins, beverage dispensing nozzles, and enclosed components of equipment such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, beverage and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending equipment at a frequency specified by the manufacturer or at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. EHS discussed with management and he will clean it within 3 days.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: there were three packages of slaw mix on the main cold rail which were 55F and the sour cream was 46F for 30 minutes. This was most likely due to the products being stacked too high in the containers.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. The EHS discussed not stocking food containers too full on the cold rail. The manager moved the products to the walk-in and decreased the amount of food in the containers. UNCLE JULIO'S RIO GRANDE CAFE (Inspection Date: 08/26/2025) Page 2 of 4

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: a container of salsa at the wait station was removed from cold holding and placed under time as a public health control without an expiration sticker for one hour.
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to- eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. The manager placed a sticker on the product.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Working containers of poisonous and toxic materials are not properly labeled with a common name. There were several unlabeled spray bottles of cleaning chemicals in the kitchen and wait station areas.
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. The manager labeled the bottles during this visit.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: 1) LARGE BATCHES OF ROASTED SALSA WERE OBSERVED COVERED AND IN THE PROCESS OF COOLING INSIDE THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EHS DISCUSSED BETTER COOLING METHODS WITH THE MANAGER. FOOD WAS MOVED TO THE WALK-IN FREEZER, UNCOVERED, AND SHALLOW PORTIONS.

out_items.name: Thermometers provided and accurate

violations.title: Thermometers, Location for Units with TCS foods
violations.observation: There was no temperature measuring device located in the following cold or hot holding equipment: the bar refrigerator used for storing cut watermelon, and the 2 drawer Delfield refrigerator under the hood.
violations.corrective_action: Cold or hot holding equipment used for the storage of time/temperature control for safety food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one integral or permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display. The manager placed new thermometers in these units during the inspection.

out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: the spray bottle at the tortilla machine was not labeled.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. The manager labeled the spray bottle during the inspection.

out_items.name: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

violations.title: Openings Protected from Pest Entry
violations.observation: Openings to the exterior of the building are present along the back door. There was a visible gap at the base of the back door which needs to be sealed to prevent pest entry.
violations.corrective_action: Fill or close holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings to protect against the entry of insects and rodents. EHS discussed with management. Ensure correction before the next inspection.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Ice As Coolant Not Used as Food
violations.observation: Ice at the bar was being used as a medium for cooling the exterior surfaces of food is also for beverage ice or used as food.
violations.corrective_action: After use as a medium for cooling the exterior surfaces of food, packaged foods, beverages, or cooling coils/tubes, the ice may not be used as food. The EHS discussed this with manager and the manager discussed it with the food employee at the bar. The cooling foods were removed and the ice was replaced. The ice will be used for food from now on.

out_items.name: Personal cleanliness

violations.title: Jewelry
violations.observation: Employees observed wearing jewelry, watches or bracelets on their arms and hands while preparing food.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall limit their jewelry to a plain wedding ring while preparing food. Food employees may not wear bracelets, watches, etc. because they can inhibit proper hand washing. The EHS discussed this with the manager. Ensure staff are trained before the next inspection.

violations.title: Hair Restraints
violations.observation: Employees observed working in the food service area without proper hair restraints. The employee making tortillas was not wearing a hair restraint.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wear hair restraints such as hats, visors, hair nets or beard nets to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and unwrapped single-service items. This section does not apply to food employees such as counter staff who ONLY serve beverages and wrapped or packaged foods, hostesses, and wait staff. This was corrected during the inspection. UNCLE JULIO'S RIO GRANDE CAFE (Inspection Date: 08/26/2025) Page 3 of 4

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: there were several instances of bowls being used to dispense ingredients, which does not prevent bare hand contact with foods.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. The manager removed the bowls in each instance.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equip/Utensils/Linens Stored off Floor, Clean Location
violations.observation: Observed equipment and other miscellaneous items stored directly on the floor in the outside storage unit.
violations.corrective_action: Store clean equipment, utensils, and linens in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. EHS discussed that the items shall be at least 6 inches off the floor. Ensure correction before the next inspection.

violations.title: Equipment/Utensils Air Drying
violations.observation: Observed several pans and other equipment stacked in the clean equipment area were still wet.
violations.corrective_action: After cleaning and sanitizing, equipment and utensils shall be air-dried or used after adequate draining before contact with food. EHS discussed with management to ensure staff are trained on allowing air drying of cleaned and sanitized equipment. Ensure correction before the next inspection.

violations.title: Plumbing System, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: The hot water on the food prep sink at the reheat station was leaking.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair. Repair the leak before the next inspection.

violations.observation: Observed the following in poor repair: 1) Kitchen area floor tiles missing grout, 2) Gaps in some ceiling panels around the dish washer vent, 3) Damaged wall in the walk-in refrigerator.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: observed cook-chill packaged with use by date of 5/12/25.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. CFM discarded package.

out_items.name: Compliance with variance, specialized process, HACCP

violations.title: ROP, HACCP Plan in Place
violations.observation: The establishment does not have an approved HACCP plan for the food that is packaged using the Reduced Oxygen Packaging (ROP) process. - OBSERVED ROP ITEMS (POBLANO SAUCE, HOT SAUCE, REFRIED BEANS) NOT ON APPROVED HACCP PLAN SUBMITTED TO HD.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment that packages a time/temperature control for safe food using a Reduced Oxygen Packaging method shall have a HACCP plan that contains the information specified under 8-201.14(D) and that: 1) identifies the food to be packaged, 2) requires that the packaged food shall be maintained at 41F or less, has a water activity of 0.91 or less, a pH of 4.6 or less, is a meat or poultry product that is cured at a food processing plant, is received in an intact package, or is a food with a high level of competing organisms, 3) describes how the package shall be prominently and conspicuosly labeled on the principal display panel in bold type on a contrasting background with instructions to maintain the food at 41F or below and discard the food if within 14 calendar days of its packaging, 40 limits the refrigerated shelf life to no more than 14 calendar days from packaging to consumption or the origjnal manufacturer's 'sell by' or 'use by' date whichever occurs first, 5) includes operational procedures that prohibit contacting food with bare hands, identifies a designated work area and the method by which physical barriers or methods of separation minimizes cross contamination, access to the processing equipment is limited to responsible trained personnel, and cleaning and sanitizing procedures for equipment/utensils is monitored, and 6) describes the training program that ensures that the individual responsible for the ROP operation understands the concepts required for a safe operation, understands the equipment and facilites, and procedures specified in this section. CFM TO REACH OUT TO CORPORATE FOR MOST UPDATED HACCP PLAN - TO INCLUDE ALL ITEMS ROP’D IN WIC. EHS WILL FOLLW UP IN 10 DAYS.
